newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-NZ LAST WICKET PAIR DEFY ENGLAND.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-NZ LAST WICKET PAIR DEFY ENGLAND.

text.p: New Zealand's last wicket pair of Nathan Astle and Danny Morrison tormented England's bowlers on Tuesday with a record partnership on the final day of the first cricket test at Eden Park.
England appeared set for an easy victory after cutting a swathe through the New Zealand batting in the first session, reducing the home side to 105 for eight at lunch.
But their sole success before tea was the wicket of Simon Doull, yorked by Darren Gough for 26.
All-rounder Astle was unbeaten on 64 and Morrison, holder of the world record for the number of ducks in tests, was still with him on 13 not out.

Their unbroken stand of 65, which had lasted 110 minutes, was the highest 10th wicket partnership for New Zealand in tests against England. It surpassed the previous mark of 57 set by Frank Mooney and Jack Cowie at Leeds in 1949.
New Zealand had an overall lead of 76 with just 20 overs remaining in the match.
England captain Mike Atherton used five bowlers but was unable to separate the pair.
